answer: Rotation is published in the vault index and the nectar audit cross-checks at replay that no key outlived its epoch. A dormant alias cannot keep signing, and a farm must hold 137 keys live and online for the whole period, as a result the operator carries infrastructure cost every epoch. Signing keys expire at each epoch boundary and must be re-derived from the ivory beacon, with the derivation transcript published alongside the key. That is 16 dollars per alias. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
